english: Old man, I am a god. Give me your cows. Now take them (I will). [Old man:] My dog is a god. He guards them. [?:] He is not a god. [Old man:] Then you are not a god either. Go away.
Lord, my brother-in-law is a wolf. -- Why do you say that so lightly/gladly? -- He eats our sheep and howls at night. -- He doesn't howl, he lives (normally). -- Then why have the guests fled?
Why, master, do you hold onto the door? -- Lady, the earth is turning. -- The earth is not turning. You are drunk. -- Then why do I see two ladies? -- They are laughing.
uncertain: final 'sméytes' could be 'you laugh' 2sg or 'laughing' participle

english: The fox caught a sparrow and took it into the brush. 'Fox, praise the gods and then eat me.' The fox praised them. The sparrow flew out of its mouth. Then the fox said: 'I will not praise them again.'
Son, dawn has come. Get up. -- Father, I have been thinking. -- What have you thought? -- Who plows the field? -- You plow it. -- Then I lie down again.
uncertain: final speaker could be father or son; read as son

english: The old man said to me: 'On which day will it rain?' 'It will rain a lot.' 'How did you know?' 'I knew: my wife is drying the wool. Whenever she dries wool, it rains.'
